elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any liquidated damages or other liquidated amount.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly makes the Termination Payment a “liquidated amount payable by the Company.”

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any penalty.
elements.evidence: No separate penalty is imposed in the rendered language; the Termination Payment is characterized as an early-termination fee and liquidated amount.

elements.element: The fee is payable by Customer only as an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (a) triggers the payment when the Company terminates the Agreement, and the added sentence expressly characterizes the Termination Payment as an “early termination fee.”

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that the Termination Payment is “capped at three (3) months' fees payable by the Company under Section 3.1 preceding the Termination Date.” This cap limits the otherwise applicable trailing-Net-Sales formula.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly states that the Termination Payment “is the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement.”

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because it retains an express liquidated payment obligation. It achieves the fallback by characterizing the payment as an early-termination fee, capping it at three months' Section 3.1 fees, and making it the sole liquidated amount. The change is minimal and leaves the payment schedule and underlying formula operative subject to the cap. Drafting quality is reduced because the original mandatory twelve-month Net Sales formula remains unchanged rather than being expressly made subject to a “lesser of” formulation, creating avoidable interpretive tension with the later cap.
